title: The ULTIMATE Abs Exercises Tier-List (Greek God-tier to Scrawny-tier)
summary: NH ranks about 40 core exercises for abs, obliques and serratus by stretch, effective range of motion and loadability. Hip flexor involvement is not a flaw, and spinal flexion and twisting are safe. His S-tier picks are decline sit-ups, oblique extensions, hanging knee raises, kneeling cable crunches, unsupported incline sit-ups, serratus punches, cannonball crunches, landmine twists, dragon flags and barbell rollouts.
claims: 'Abs are made in the kitchen' is idiotic; like any muscle, abs are built in the gym and need direct training
Rejecting ab exercises because they recruit hip flexors is wrong; muscles work together and the hip flexors move the body so the abs can stabilise and stretch
Bending and twisting the spine is a natural function of the core and safe unless you're reckless
Ab exercise criteria: a good stretch, high effective range of motion, and ease of loading and progressing; abs need progressive overload too
Being skinny with a six-pack doesn't count; you want a developed core on a big body
Crunches are bad mainly because of tiny range of motion and minimal stretch, not because of lower back danger
Planks teach novices to brace, but they become redundant, the arms tire first, and compound lifts already give isometric core work
Lifters with advanced physiques were obsessed with sit-ups at some point; not optimal, but they work thanks to the stretch
Decline bench sit-ups are ideal: stable, good stretch and negative, loadable from bodyweight up to 60-70 lb, but control the negative to avoid tearing
Barbell side bends or twists and dumbbell side bends train obliques poorly: momentum, poor range of motion and needless spinal loading
Twisting suits oblique development better than side bending
Calisthenics athletes have good abs because they are lean and because stabilisation produces some hypertrophy; skills like the planche result from strong abs rather than causing them
More range of motion isn't always better; effective range of motion is what matters, so hanging leg raises beat toes-to-bar
Hanging leg and knee raises bias the lower abs because the abs stretch to catch the legs on the negative, even though lower abs can't be isolated
Bending the knees shortens the lever, improves pelvic rotation and ab engagement; 10-12 clean knee raises with slow negatives means well-developed abs
Fat burners don't work, and without developed abs underneath you just get a poor six-pack
Ab twister machines lock the hips and force unnatural spinal twisting; twisting should involve the hips and feet
Standing cable crunches become a noob trap where body weight does the work; kneeling cable crunches fix this and are one of the best ab exercises
CoolSculpting, liposuction and ab implants reinforce bad habits; lose the fat and train the core
A well-developed core correlates with lower mortality: less visceral fat, longer mobility and a healthier spine
Compounds alone are not enough for ab development, but pull-ups, squats and deadlifts train the core through stabilisation and anti-bending, especially the obliques
Unilateral loading like suitcase deadlifts hits the obliques harder with less weight
Even at higher body fat on a bulk he has some serratus because he trains it; serratus functions are protraction and upward scapular rotation, and training it helps shoulder issues
Serratus uppercuts and scapular-plane raises mostly train the shoulders; pullovers help but the serratus is never the limiting factor
He rehabbed broken ribs by strengthening and thickening his serratus with serratus punches
The burn is not a variable of hypertrophy
Bicycle crunches look hard and tax cardio but give poor results; don't train to impress others
Windshield wipers waste about half their range of motion and are hard to load; Russian twists are better
The hollow body position and L-sit give free ab hypertrophy when applied passively to push-ups and pull-ups; at 215 lb he can hold an L-sit
Ab circuits of 30 reps per exercise fail: no progressive overload, poor intensity, no adherence; dragon flags twice a week for a year beat circuits done for two weeks
Standard ab wheel rollouts lock the grip narrow and prevent scapular motion, which can hurt shoulders; barbell rollouts let you choose grip width
With 20+ A or S tier options there is no excuse not to train abs directly; pick ones you enjoy for consistency
